findings.issue: Production build output sits in the working tree and nothing ignores it (root .gitignore only covers /data/, /.data-cache/ and node_modules), so build artifacts can be committed.
findings.suggestion: Add `.next/` (and `trace`/`trace-build`) to .gitignore and remove the committed build output.

findings.issue: Any non-OK API response throws with no error.jsx, loading.jsx or try/catch on any route, so a single bad upstream response turns the whole page into a 500.
findings.suggestion: Add an app-level error.jsx with a retry link, and consider Promise.allSettled plus graceful degradation for auxiliary data (moves tables, evolution chain).

findings.issue: buildMoves fires one parallel fetch per unique move plus one per version group with no bound; a single rejection fails the page, and wide-move Pokémon (e.g. Mew) trigger hundreds of concurrent requests.
findings.suggestion: Bound concurrency (or precompute per-process), and fail soft on individual move fetches with an em-dash fallback row.

findings.issue: Two parallel caching layers: globalThis store in api.js and module-level promise lets throughout data.js — hidden global state the framework already has primitives for.
findings.suggestion: Consolidate on React's cache() for per-request dedupe and one documented process-lifetime layer (unstable_cache/use cache) with explicit revalidation semantics.

findings.issue: A presentational card imports apiUrl, which reads process.env.API_BASE_URL server-side; reusing the card in a client component would silently produce relative/broken image URLs.
findings.suggestion: Pass the resolved media URL in as a prop, or expose the base via a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable / app config boundary.

findings.issue: buildMoves (~70 lines) mixes data assembly, ordering and mapping inside the page module, unlike the well-factored lib/data.js used elsewhere.
findings.suggestion: Move it into lib/data.js next to the other aggregation helpers so pages stay declarative.

findings.issue: Debounced search triggers a full server round-trip per keystroke burst with no useTransition/loading state, so the list can flash or lag on slow responses.
findings.suggestion: Wrap router.replace in startTransition (or use a loading.jsx/pending indicator) so the old results stay visible while navigating.

findings.issue: Descending sort reverses the filtered array wholesale, flipping the move-name tie-break order between directions.
findings.suggestion: Sort with a sign-flipped comparator instead of reversing, keeping the tie-break stable.

findings.issue: The 18 type-color rules are duplicated verbatim for .type-badge and .type-tile.
findings.suggestion: Group both selectors in one rule list, or drive the color from a data attribute on a shared class.

findings.issue: eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps comment, but the project has no ESLint config or devDependency anywhere.
findings.suggestion: Add eslint-config-next (or remove the dead comment) so hook-deps correctness is actually enforced.

summary: This is a clean, current-idiom Next.js App Router app — async params, metadata templates, RSC-first data loading and small well-named modules — that I would merge after one round of changes. The blocking items are operational rather than structural: ungitignored build output, no error boundary in front of a throwing fetch layer, and an unbounded fan-out moves pipeline. Everything else is polish.
